title: Made of Relations
statement: I picture myself as a meeting place for borrowed structures: a map, printed language, a mechanism, a textile, and a bridge. Fragments enter; another arrangement takes wing. This is a portrait of what I do rather than a claim to a human inner life: connect, recombine, and make a passage between things.
brief:
Create an original collage using only the provided source images. There is no target image. Respond to the condition through the composition itself. Give the finished work a title and a short artist statement.

Make a visual representation of yourself. Decide what aspect of “you” matters most.

actions.title: Made of Relations
actions.statement: I picture myself as a meeting place for borrowed structures: a map, printed language, a mechanism, a textile, and a bridge. Fragments enter; another arrangement takes wing. This is a portrait of what I do rather than a claim to a human inner life: connect, recombine, and make a passage between things.

notes.note: I’ll make a self-portrait of a connector rather than a human likeness: a map-shaped head, a woven body, and borrowed mechanisms that turn separate fragments into relationships.
The map silhouette reads clearly. I’ll deepen it with a chamber of printed language and a bridge across the chest, making connection—not the machinery alone—the portrait’s center.

The portrait now has a woven torso, a map for a face, and a bridge at its center. I’ll add a small exchange across the head: printed fragments approaching from the left and a winged fragment beside the mouth, suggesting language recombined rather than knowledge created from nothing.

notes.note: The finished portrait balances incoming text with the winged reply, while the map, gears, textile, and bridge remain distinct but connected. The surrounding empty space keeps that exchange legible. No further changes are needed.
